items.framing_of_record:
DIRECTOR RULING 2026-09-05, correcting this build's own first statement of it. BF-1 is an INSTRUMENT DISAGREEMENT RESOLVED BY AN INDEPENDENT EXPECTATION -- NOT 'the product is now right, therefore the check may be retired'.

The distinction is not stylistic. W5 and the product disagree about what an incoming typed edge should say. The product's correctness is precisely what is in dispute, so citing it to justify retiring the check that disputes it argues in a circle, and a build that can retire a failing acceptance check by asserting its own correctness has no acceptance gate at all.

What resolves the disagreement is a THIRD PARTY: tools/l4_direction_oracle.py holds EXPECTED_SENTENCES written by hand from CONSTRAINTS O8 and not imported from explorer.models, a property a committed test asserts. It compared 5,052 edges and found 0 defects -- agreeing with the product's rendering and against W5's expectation. W5 cannot arbitrate, because its expectation IS the constant in dispute. The product's correctness is the CONCLUSION of that comparison, never its premise; had the oracle disagreed, W5's FAIL would stand.

INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED by critic round 2 (S8-CR2), 2026-09-05, which verified rather than accepted the claim: it checked both flagged sentences against CONSTRAINTS O8 itself, traced the mechanism to probe_corpus_explorer.py:1956-1962 and the RELATION_LABELS import at :151, and considered whether the check could have been retired dishonestly -- concluding not, because the failure was accepted in writing at c861680 BEFORE round 6 was dispatched rather than discovered afterwards and rationalised, the preset was left failing rather than edited green, and the compensating control was built and run.

items.measured_cause:
MEASURED, not inferred, from the probe's own capture at the Director's instruction. A pixel scan of W1.png found content beyond x=1280 on exactly THREE sampled rows, y 1881-1887, reaching x=1386 -- a single ~7 px band, one line of content, nothing else on a 6,624 px page. W9 is the same shape at y 1851-1857. Cropping and reading that band identifies it directly: it is the CARD PANEL's `Card sha256` value, the 64-character hex string, rendered at reader.html:132 as `
{{ view.card_row.card_sha256 }}
`. Why the round-8 repair could not move it: app.css:153 applies the wrapping recipe (white-space: pre-wrap; overflow-wrap: anywhere; word-break: break-word) to `pre`, and :172 applies it to `.doc-body table td`. Those are the two mechanisms critic round 1 named as 'likely causes, not isolated'. The actual element is a bare ``, which app.css:142 gives a monospace font and NO wrapping rule, and which reader.css does not style at all -- it contains no `code`, `overflow-wrap` or `word-break` rule anywhere. An unbreakable 64-character token in an unwrapped inline element overflows its box, and nothing clips it. The reader's own layout is otherwise correct and was never the problem: `.reader-layout` uses minmax(0, 2fr)/minmax(0, 1fr), both `#document` and `#card-panel` carry min-width: 0, and `.source-scroll` has overflow-x: auto. The build fixed the mechanisms it was told about and the element that overflows was a third one nobody measured.

critic_round_2.convergence_reasoning_summary:
The critic declined the literal reading and said why. PROMPT.md section 7's 'unchanged ranked issue set' rule was written to detect a fixed point in a build that MAY OR MAY NOT act. When a build accepts and acts on every item, the rule INVERTS: an unchanged set would mean the repairs did not take (the worst outcome) and a changed set means they did (the best), so the rule can no longer distinguish 'converged' from 'still improving'.

Its substitute reading: convergence means the CLASS distribution of findings is stable and no longer regenerating. Round 1's classes were (a) direction prose stating the converse of the record, (b) a claim in prose that nothing checks against the artifact, (c) layout and keyboard polish, (d) a check narrower than its apparent guarantee. Round 2: (a) is gone at the mechanism. (c) persists with its principal instance unmoved. (d) persists one degree smaller. And (b) HAS PRODUCED THREE NEW INSTANCES INSIDE ARTIFACTS CREATED AFTER ROUND 1 IN RESPONSE TO IT -- an oracle report saying 213 pages were rendered when none was; a comment claiming no raw SQL directly above raw SQL; and a ledger asserting all five sealed items closed while carrying still_live: true on one.

'The sealed audit named class (b) as this harness's structural weakness. The build read that, repaired every named instance, and reproduced the class in the instruments it built to end it. That is not a fixed point. A build that reproduces the critic's named defect class inside the compensating controls for that class is still generating, not converging.'

The SA-4 closure claim is the integrator's ledger entry. Recorded plainly because the M3 ANL's question is whether the harness can audit its own claims, and the answer this round is that it could not, in the very act of building the instruments meant to prove it could.

terminal_state.prompt_section_12_reasoning:
PROMPT.md section 12 permits PASS only if, among other things, all objective gates pass, production-path probes pass, and 'critic score reaches 8.5 if the critic scale was validly usable'.

All nine objective gates pass, independently re-assessed by critic round 2 with no disagreement -- including gate 7, which the build had asserted falsely, the critic FAILED, the build then withdrew, repaired, and evidenced at L4.

The critic scale was NOT validly usable, so the 8.5 clause is vacuous and cannot license or block anything. This is stated so that nobody reads the ref_score of 8 as the cause of this terminal state. It is not.

What is dispositive is the unconditional requirement that PRODUCTION-PATH PROBES PASS. They do not: the acceptance set is 11 of 12, with W5 red. W5's failure is understood, declared in advance, verified to be the declared failure and only that, and resolved as an instrument disagreement in the product's favour by an independent oracle -- but section 12 does not offer a category for 'a required bar unmet for a well-understood reason'. It offers exactly one: BOUNDED_FAIL, 'the application is usable but a required bar remains unmet after convergence or budget exhaustion'. Both conditions hold: the probe's budget is exhausted at 4 of 4 and was explicitly not waived, and critic round 2 determined NOT CONVERGED.

Declaring PASS here would require reading the acceptance set as 12 of 12 on the ground that the one red preset is wrong. That is the reading the Director's BF-1 ruling forbids, and forbids for the right reason: a build that can retire a failing acceptance check by declaring the check wrong has no acceptance gate at all.
